status: design only; current work is diagnostic counting, sparse traversal is not implemented
baseline_compatible_objects: cycles11/inline_timers_objects.txt; earlier object caches are layout-incompatible
scope: First timer parent scan only. Preserve character physics timers, buff ticks, opponent/fatigue/player phase order, parent/gem order and all original tick bodies.
criteria: Skip only parents with empty own timer array and no nonnull gem having a nonempty timer array. Keep stopped timers in eligible parents, so same-frame start/stop/restart needs no flag-index tracking.
tracking: GdArr private sticky bit in padding. Mark item timer/gem arrays at init and property setters, final wrapper gem array, and captured inventory array at phase entry. Every mutation through any array alias invalidates a saturating thread-local epoch. All direct timer/gem field assignments must be audited and instrumented.
hot_path: Cache ascending physical slot indices per CoreCharacter, keyed by captured items pointer, captured length, epoch and battle generation/context. Raw uint32 index storage in arena; no std::vector in arena because destructors are not run. Rebuild only when invalid. Preserve old captured array reference if inventory field changes.
dirty_midpass: Process original body at each eligible index. After a callback changes epoch, resume original dense traversal at last processed physical index+1, through the original captured length. Never resume only cached indices after mutation.
one_body: Use one processing body and a cursor selector; avoid duplicating large timer/gem bodies in indexed/dense paths. Snapshot indices pointer/count/epoch into locals before processing so callbacks or nested phases cannot overwrite outer loop metadata.
unknown_values: Eligibility reads must be side-effect free: conservatively include non-Obj/null/unowned/non-CoreItem slots, malformed array fields and unknown cases. Use arena ownership before dereferencing future pointers. Generated native metadata getters are pure; outside the internal bridge flag, retain original dense path to preserve custom C++ getter/callback behavior.
reentry: Formal code should have thread-local kernel depth guard: nested phases use original dense path and do not rebuild shared caches. sort_custom invokes callbacks while mutating; use a scoped callback-mutation busy guard (including initially untracked arrays) and invalidate at end if tracked. During busy mutation, use dense traversal. Other GdArr mutators have no script callbacks, but audit all native runtime array mutation paths.
epoch_cost: Capture a pointer/reference to TLS scan state once per phase, not a TLS lookup per item. Check ordinary state->epoch between eligible parents. Saturate UINT64_MAX and permanently use dense fallback there; avoid ABA wrap.
lifetime: Reset cache metadata in CoreCharacter.init_fields. Context/gid_epoch distinguishes battle resets. Normal bridge items are arena-owned and thread-confined; external/default contexts retain original behavior.
tests: Differential fast-vs-original fallback with captured length, append/remove/shrink/reorder/replace arrays, alias mutations, same-frame gem insertion, new timers, start/stop/restart/first-pass eligibility, nested kernel calls, sort callbacks, invalid future placeholders repaired before visit, and unchanged external custom getters. New header fields require a fresh full 20-unit build and recompiled C++ test executables.
pipeline_composition: Inline timer pass currently guards entire four files against original hashes. A later accepted tracking/cache layer requires safe versioned allowed normalized hashes or verified own-region idempotence before wiring both passes. Keep sparse flag declaration BEFORE existing inline FLAG block; reset line AFTER inline reset line; wrapper enable AFTER inline enable; timer mark AFTER the complete existing inline NEW_ASSIGN block. This preserves byte order under inline normalization/reapplication.
release: Fixed 200, two independent 8-pair isolated 60s-warm AB/BA groups (third if unclear), full 2604 strict originals plus unchanged per-case C++ event hashes, raw 24 batches all >=50, power/load report, load20 only within observed range, normal training and manifest/DLL SHA checks. Commit/push verified state before each risky change.
